messages:
raj: Heads-up: Customer Opal needs BYOK with an on-prem HSM located in SG and wants a local subcontractor that can perform emergency "rewraps" under SLA. They asked for a clear custody boundary + RBAC matrix.
haley: Ok. Key legal note: any subprocessor in SG triggers cross-border data transfer and consent. Also need to map what we actually allow them to do (submit, approve, or perform cryptographic ops).
morgan: Customer text: "local operator to perform rewraps under customer-approved process". They specifically asked the subprocessor can run a rewrap in emergencies, but not hold unwrapped key material.
raj: Proposal: do NOT give subprocessor direct HSM key material. Build a rewrap-proxy that performs an ephemeral session in the customer's HSM (customer HSM generates a short-lived wrapping key used only for the operation). Operator submits a rewrap job, the proxy opens an attested session, performs unwrap/rewrap, returns attestation and hashes.
haley: Compliance checklist we need: (a) operator identity + justification logged, (b) attestation blob from HSM per operation, (c) non-export of key material in logs, (d) data residency proof that key doesn't leave customer's HSM except wrapped outputs. Can our audit pipeline capture attestation blobs?
morgan: Yes. We'll store attestation blobs as binary artifacts in the audit-store, reference them with a digest in the audit log. The log entry should contain: rewrap_id, operator_id, request_reason, attestation_digest, input_ciphertext_hash, output_ciphertext_hash, firmware_version. No raw keys.
secbot: Draft IAM role suggestion:
```
- name: subprocessor.rewraper
  allowed_actions: ["rewrap:submit","rewrap:approve","rewrap:status"]
  forbidden_actions: ["kms:exportKey","kms:listKeys","kms:importKey"]
  enforcement: ["mfa", "webauthn", "justification_tag"]
```
haley: Good. Also require time-limited access tokens tied to operator certs and a per-operation justification that is auditable. Legal will insist on consent + SOW appendix per customer for subprocessors.
raj: For KMS/HSM integration pattern: two options we support: 
1) Ephemeral wrapping session inside customer HSM (preferred): proxy negotiates a session, HSM derives ephemeral wrapping key, no persistent custody.
2) Escrow pattern: the customer provides a wrapped rewrap-authority key under M-of-N control; the proxy uses it only if multiple approvers sign. This is heavier and needs escrow policy.
morgan: Ephemeral session avoids long-term custody so better for compliance. Implementation note: HSM needs to support sealed sessions and sign attestations that include session nonce + operator id.
haley: Retention: customer wants 5-10 years for some regulated audits; our default is 1 year. We should support per-customer retention labels for rewrap audit records and route to cold storage with access controls. Make sure PII minimization is enforced (no operator biometrics, etc).
raj: Oncall/resilience: what happens if a rewrap fails mid-stream during DR? Define runbook: operator retries via proxy; if attestation mismatch or checksum fails -> immediately escalate to sec oncall. Also create an automated incident when rewrap_checksum != expected_hash.
oncall-sre: I'll add a playbook: step 1: block further rewraps, step 2: gather attestation blobs, step 3: run reproducibility test in staging HSM, step 4: contact customer operator and legal if mismatch. Add an incident tag `rewrap-integrity-failure`.
morgan: Vulnerability threat model: replay attacks, forged requests, operator credential compromise. Controls: nonce per request, short TTL signatures from operator cert, HSM-side check of nonce freshness, per-request monotonically increasing rewrap counter logged inside HSM attestation. Add SIEM detection for duplicate nonces or counter jumps.
haley: Also require code signing + runtime integrity for proxy binary. If proxy compromise is suspected, auditors will want evidence of code-signing checks and attestation chain.
secbot: SIEM rules added: 
- rewrap_nonce_replay -> severity=high -> auto-open incident channel
- rewrap_counter_jump -> severity=critical -> pager to sec-oncall
- rewrap_attestation_mismatch -> severity=high -> create case in IR tracker
raj: One more: RBAC change process. We'll need a short-lived feature flag for the new role, and a migration plan for existing subprocessors. Morgan, can you open an IAM PR with tests that assert forbidden_actions are enforced?
morgan: Yep, I'll add unit/integration tests that attempt forbidden APIs (kms:exportKey) and expect 403. PR by EOD tomorrow.
haley: Legal & privacy: I'll draft the SOW appendix and the customer consent flow (checkbox + signed appendix). Also add export-control checklist for SG.
raj: Nice. Let's aim to demo the proxy rewrap flow with a synthetic HSM attestation to Opal next week. Anything else?
oncall-sre: I'll schedule a short tabletop for oncall tomorrow to run the rewrap failure drill. I'll include steps for evidence collection and legal notification.
morgan: I'll also add telemetry: per-rewrap latency, success rate, attestation verification time. Helps ops/SRE tune timeouts.
haley: tagging @legal-team and @sales-ops after this thread for next steps.
secbot: Policy enforcement reminder: all rewraps must attach attestation blob or request will be rejected. :lock:
raj: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with PR links in this channel. :thumbsup:
